transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... people keep acting like I'm just imagining things. But I know what's going on. The hospital people and some folks from the agency, they've been watching our house. They even watch my cleaning routes when I'm out working, just to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband.
How long have you been feeling like you are being watched by these people?
Well, it's been going on for a while now. The feeling that they're watching us... and the voices, too... it's been about 11 months since all of this started.

Have you experienced any periods where your mood felt extremely low, or perhaps unusually elevated or energetic, that lasted for a significant portion of the time you've been dealing with these voices and feelings of being watched?

Well, mostly I've just been... really keyed up. I wouldn't say I've felt low, but for most of this whole change over the last year, I've been very irritable and just driven to keep moving. It's like I can't stop. Even in the stretches when things weren't at their worst with the watching and the voices, I still had this constant need to just stay in motion and keep busy.
During those times when you felt unusually irritable and driven to stay in motion, did you ever need much less sleep than usual while still feeling fully energized?

Yes, actually. Many nights I'll only sleep for maybe... two or three hours. But I wake up completely ready to go. I'll just get right up and start scrubbing floors or sorting through papers. I'm not tired at all, not like I used to be after a short night. I just wake up and I'm ready to get to work.

Looking back over the entire 11 months, would you say that these periods of feeling 'keyed up,' irritable, and needing very little sleep have been present for most of that time, or did they only happen during shorter, specific episodes?

Yeah, like I was saying before... it's really been for most of this whole change. It wasn't just short little episodes here and there. 

Pretty much this entire time, I've been keyed up and irritable, just completely driven to keep moving and getting things done. Even during the stretches when the other things—the voices and the feeling of being watched—weren't at their absolute worst, I still couldn't just sit down and rest. It's been going on for the majority of these 11 months.
During those 11 months, would you say that the periods where you were feeling 'keyed up' and needing very little sleep were present for the majority of the total time you have been ill?

Yes, like I just said, that's exactly right. For most of this whole change, I have been keyed up and irritable. I'm just driven to keep moving, cleaning, doing whatever. Even in the stretches when things were not at their worst with the other stuff, I was still like that for the vast majority of the time.

During those 11 months, were there any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced the voices and the feeling of being watched, but were not feeling 'keyed up' or having that constant need to stay in motion?

Yes, there was a time like that. Um... I remember a quieter spell that lasted for a few weeks. I was actually sleeping a bit more then, and I wasn't rushing around cleaning quite as much. But even during that time, I was still hearing the voice by the kitchen window. And I still knew the agency was keeping an eye on us. So the keyed-up feeling settled down for a bit, but the other things were still there.
